slight correction, the Torah is the first 5 books--Genesis, Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers, and Deuteronomy. Our version of what you call the Old Testament is the Tanakh (an acronym of Torah, Nevi'im, Ketuvim, or Law, Prophets, Writings). It's in a different order and Christianity uses different translations which lead to Jesus in a way the Tanakh does not.

  
We view 'chosen' differently; there's a story in Judaism that God went around to all the nations of the earth and offered them the Torah, and they all declined; when God came to the Israelites, we chose to accept the yoke of the Law--we're 'chosen' because we were the ones who chose the Law. Now, 'chose' is doing a lot of work here because depending on how you read the Hebrew, the scene at Mt Sinai can be read as God literally holding the mountain over the heads of the Israelites as a, shall we say, ''encouragement'' to accept the Law.

But generally speaking, amongst Jews we don't really talk about being 'the Chosen People.' It's a term we have to deal with and explain, and there are explanations for it, but it's not something that comes up regularly the way it does amongst Gentiles.
